items.title: Raw jujube stone and raw hawthorn stone particles as green adsorbents for the adsorption of different organic dyes
items.authors: Mousavi SH, Jafari S, Hanifehpour S, Moafi HF.
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, the raw jujube stone particles (RJSP) and the raw hawthorn stone particles (RHSP) as efficient natural and green adsorbents were used for the adsorption of methylene blue (MB), malachite green (MG), crystal violet (CV), and disperse red 1 (DR1) dyes. The functional groups, morphology, particle size, surface area, and pore size of RJSP and RHSP were determined using FT-IR, BET, FESEM, TEM, and EDX. The green adsorbents RJSP and RHSP showed high efficiency in the adsorption of MB, MG, CV, and DR1 dyes and showed comparable performance to other reported adsorbents. According to the results, the adsorption of MB, MG, CV, and DR1 dyes onto RJSP and RHSP follows the Freundlich isotherm, while the kinetics are well described by the pseudo-second-order model. Also, according to the Langmuir isotherm, RJSP exhibited maximum adsorption capacities (Q m ) of 145, 124, 114, and 98 mg/g for MB, MG, CV, and DR1, respectively, while RHSP showed adsorption capacities of 84, 111, 102, and 94 mg/g. In addition, thermodynamic parameters confirm that the adsorption of MB, MG, CV, and DR1 dyes is exothermic on RJSP and endothermic on RHSP. Finally, the RJSP and RHSP can be used as affordable, environmentally friendly, and effective natural adsorbents for the removal of various industrial dyes.

items.title: Optimization of water chestnut starch-based encapsulation systems for improved probiotic survival under simulated gastrointestinal stress
items.authors: Farhan Saeed, Aftab Ahmed, Nameer Khairullah Mohammed, Nighat Raza, Laraib Shoukat, Huda Ateeq
items.abstract: The present study aimed to improve the viability and stability of probiotic bacteria under adverse environmental and gastrointestinal conditions through encapsulation in water chestnut starch-based micro- and nanoparticles prepared by the gelation method. The resulting particles were characterized and evaluated for their ability to protect Bifidobacterium bifidum during storage, thermal exposure, and simulated gastrointestinal conditions. Both encapsulation systems demonstrated high encapsulation yields, with values of 95% and 97% for microcapsules and nanocapsules, respectively. During storage, encapsulated probiotics exhibited significantly greater viability than free cells. After 20 days, viable counts decreased from approximately 9.50 log CFU/g to 7.29 log CFU/g in microencapsulated cells, and 8.94 log CFU/g in nanoencapsulated cells. Encapsulation also enhanced thermal stability compared with free probiotic cells. Under simulated gastric conditions, free cells showed the greatest loss in viability, decreasing to 4.74 log CFU/g after 120 min, whereas microencapsulated and nanoencapsulated cells retained viable counts of approximately 7.62 and 8.55 log CFU/g, respectively. Similarly, under simulated intestinal conditions, free cells showed the lowest survival, 3.65 log CFU/g, while encapsulated cells maintained substantially higher viability. Nanoencapsulated cells exhibited the highest survival (8.13 log CFU/g), demonstrating the protective effect of starch-based encapsulation against gastrointestinal stress. In contrast, free probiotic cells showed substantially greater losses in viability under all tested conditions. items.title: Drought resilience of Portuguese chestnut cultivars under Mediterranean rainfed conditions​.
items.authors: Marques T, Ferreira-Pinto A, Aires A, Pinto T, Gomes-Laranjo J.
items.abstract: Abstract Increasing summer drought and climatic irregularity threaten sweet chestnut production in Mediterranean regions. However, cultivar-specific drought resilience under field conditions remains insufficiently resolved because the relative roles of hydraulic status, gas exchange and biochemical adjustment are rarely evaluated together. This study aimed to characterise the drought response strategies of three traditional Portuguese chestnut cultivars, Judia, Longal and Martaínha, and the hybrid rootstock ColUTAD®, across four orchards representing a natural edaphoclimatic gradient during the 2023 growing season. Summer drought intensity was described using climatic descriptors combined with plant-based indicators of water status, particularly midday stem water potential ( Ψ wmid ) and relative water content (RWC). Across cultivar-site combinations, Ψ wmid ranged from − 1.75 to − 1.05 MPa, RWC from 78.9 to 91.9%, net photosynthesis from 4.5 to 15.0 µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹, and transpiration from 1.1 to 3.5 mmol H₂O m⁻² s⁻¹. Less negative Ψ wmid values were associated with higher RWC, photosynthesis and transpiration, whereas electrolyte leakage increased as plant water status declined. Cultivar-dependent responses were particularly evident for transpiration, instantaneous water-use efficiency, soluble sugars, electrolyte leakage and antioxidant-related traits. Martaínha showed the most favourable integrated response under the 2023 climatic configuration, combining less negative Ψ wmid , higher leaf hydration, sustained gas exchange and comparatively controlled biochemical activation. Longal displayed high physiological plasticity and strong antioxidant capacity, whereas Judia showed effective gas-exchange and biochemical responses but greater sensitivity to water limitation.…

items.title: Integrated defense strategies of Chinese chestnut against Oligonychus ununguis: coordinated regulation of morphological barriers, constitutive metabolites, and transcriptome-metabolome responses
items.authors: Xin-Fang Zhang, Ying Li, Yan Guo, Jin-Yu Liu, Jia-Yi Liu, Yu-Jie Wang
items.abstract: The multidimensional defense mechanisms of chestnut ( Castanea mollissima ) against the spider mite, Oligonychus ununguis , encompassing physical barriers, constitutive metabolites, and post-infestation responses, remain poorly characterized. This study integrated leaf micromorphology, physiological and biochemical profiling, transcriptomics, and metabolomics to elucidate the coordinated defense architecture of chestnut against O. ununguis . Leaf anatomical traits of six cultivars, comprising three resistant and three susceptible genotypes, were evaluated, while four representative cultivars were subjected to physiological-biochemical assays, widely targeted metabolomic profiling, and RNA sequencing before and 2 days after mite infestation. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and linear mixed models (LMMs) were used to characterize co-expression patterns and metabolite-morphology associations. Cultivar-specific anatomical differences were observed among cultivars: the resistant cultivar ‘Likang’ exhibited significantly greater leaf thickness and upper epidermal thickness ( P < 0.05), whereas the resistant cultivar ‘Songjiazao’ possessed a thicker wax layer than the other cultivars. Biochemical profiling revealed cultivar-specific differentiation rather than a uniform resistant-group phenotype. For example, soluble sugar content was lowest in ‘Xujia1’, whereas soluble protein content was highest in ‘Likang’; however, none of these traits varied consistently within the resistant group, while LMM identified significant associations between four biochemical indicators (soluble sugars, flavonoids, lignin and soluble protein) and leaf structural traits, consistent with putative resource-allocation trade-offs. items.title: Predicting the impact of climate change on the climatic suitability for Ziziphus jujuba in China.
items.authors: Zhao Z, Zhang J, Wu X.
items.abstract: Ziziphus jujuba Mill. is an economically valuable tree species in China, and its climatically suitable range is sensitive to future climate risks, with implications for biological resource conservation. Species occurrence records and bioclimatic variables were integrated, and a parameter-tuned MaxEnt model was employed to forecast the potential climatic suitability for Z. jujuba in China under three shared socioeconomic pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5). The adjusted model exhibited excellent predictive performance (AUC = 0.947). Annual mean temperature, precipitation seasonality, and temperature seasonality were identified as the dominant climatic drivers. Currently, highly suitable areas (8.84% of total suitable area) are concentrated in the Bohai Rim region. Under future scenarios, although the total climatically suitable area expands across all pathways, its spatial pattern undergoes significant reorganization: contraction in southeastern margins, expansion into northwestern inland regions, and relative stability in the core area. The centroid is projected to shift continuously northwestward, with a maximum cumulative migration of 504.67 km under SSP5-8.5. Future planning must prioritize the risk of declining suitability in traditional southeastern production areas and carefully assess the practical feasibility of potential expansion zones in the northwest. These findings provide a scientific basis for climate-adaptive management of Z. jujuba resources.

items.title: Quantitative Variation in Black Spot Disease Response Among Ziziphus jujuba Genotypes Assessed by Detached-Leaf and Detached-Fruit Phenotyping Against Alternaria alternata-Associated Isolate Q44
items.authors: R. Siddique, Ping Xiong, Zhi Luo, Fen-Fen Yan
items.abstract: Black spot disease associated with Alternaria alternata reduces the quality and marketability of jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) fruit; however, quantitative variation in disease response among jujube genotypes remains insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated 60 genotypes, comprising two parental genotypes and 58 F1 progenies, using complementary detached-leaf and detached-fruit assays. Isolate Q44 was characterized morphologically and placed within the A. alternata-associated clade using internal transcribed spacer sequence analysis. The assays were conducted in three independent experimental runs and analyzed using a randomized complete block design, with experimental run as the blocking factor. Genotype significantly affected detached-leaf lesion area, detached-fruit lesion area, and fruit lesion depth (p < 0.0001). Panel-relative disease indices revealed marked differences among traits: 83.33% of genotypes occurred in Grades I–II for fruit lesion area, compared with 46.67% for leaf lesion area and 30.00% for fruit lesion depth, whereas 56.67% were classified in Grades IV–V for lesion depth. Detached-leaf and detached-fruit lesion areas were strongly associated (r = 0.9015, p < 0.0001), with the fitted linear model accounting for 81.26% of the variation in fruit lesion area. The first two principal components explained 98.7% of the variation in the three measured lesion-response traits. Integrated disease-response analysis identified Q38, Q79, Q184, Q106, and Q170 as lower-response genotypes, whereas Q175, Q56, Q76, Q17, and P3X-10 exhibited higher responses. These contrasting genotypes provide useful materials for multi-isolate validation, field evaluation, and future jujube improvement studies.

items.title: Changes in Postharvest Quality and Bioactive Compounds of Jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) Fruit Harvested at Different Maturity Stages During Cold Storage
items.authors: Chul-Woo Kim, Yonghyun Kim, U. Lee, H. Eo
items.abstract: Harvest maturity, as indicated by red surface coloration, is an important determinant of postharvest quality in jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.). ‘Bokjo’ jujube fruit were harvested at three coloration stages, stage 1 (≤10% red surface), stage 2 (40–60%), and stage 3 (≥90%), and stored at 3 ± 1 °C for 8 weeks. Stage 1 and stage 2 fruit continued to develop red coloration during storage. The color difference (ΔE*ab) between stage 2 and stage 3 fruit decreased from 28.3 at harvest to 8.4 at week 8, whereas a substantial color difference remained between stage 1 and stage 3 fruit (ΔE*ab = 20.1). However, soluble solids content remained relatively stable during storage and was lower in stage 1 (21–23 °Brix) and stage 2 (23–26 °Brix) than in stage 3 fruit (29–32 °Brix). Stage 3 fruit showed the highest incidence of postharvest disorders, with cracking reaching 60% at week 4 and soft rot reaching 40% at week 8, whereas the incidence of these disorders remained at or below 15% in stages 1 and 2. Stage 1 fruit exhibited the highest flavonoid and phenolic contents and DPPH radical-scavenging activity but also showed the greatest weight loss (3.4%) and shriveling incidence (35%) at week 8. These findings suggest that harvesting at stage 2 may provide a favorable balance between fruit appearance and storage stability during extended cold storage.

items.title: Optimizing the Strategies of Ziziphus jujuba ‘Dongzao’ Irrigation with Long-Term Saline Water in Yellow River Delta, China, Using MODFLOW and HYDRUS-2D
items.authors: X. Cong, Yu-Cai Xie, Rong-Zhen Wang, Zheng-He Xu, G. Pang
items.abstract: Optimizing saline drip irrigation to protect soil conditions and maintain Ziziphus jujuba ‘Dongzao’ yield is critical for freshwater-scarce regions with shallow saline groundwater. This study incorporated groundwater table variations and their long-term effects into the irrigation scheduling optimization framework to develop a saline drip irrigation regulation pattern suitable for jujube under shallow groundwater conditions. To this end, simulated hydraulic heads from MODFLOW were used to update the bottom boundary condition of HYDRUS-2D, to quantify soil water–salt transport and optimize irrigation management. A three-year field experiment was conducted in the Yellow River Delta. Five saline drip irrigation treatments (1 (control), 2, 3, 4, and 5 g·L−1) were established to investigate their influences on soil water content, soil salinity, jujube yield and fruit quality. Based on the experimental data, the MODFLOW and HYDRUS models were then calibrated and validated to simulate different saline water irrigation scenarios over a 10-year period, and the effects on the spatiotemporal variations in water and salt transport processes were analyzed. The main results were as follows: (1) The yield exhibited an inverse relationship with irrigation water salinity, with significant yield reductions (p < 0.05) observed only at the 4 and 5 g·L−1 treatments compared to the control. (2) The relative yield declined to 50% and 85% when the average saturated paste extract electrical conductivity (ECe) of soil reached 12.64 dS·m−1 (0.27%) and 8.85 dS·m−1 (0.19%), respectively. Moderate saline irrigation improved fruit quality, and the treatment of 4 g·L−1 achieved the best performance. items.title: Shifts in Biomass Allocation and Trait Correlations Under the Combined Effects of Drought and Shade.
items.authors: Fazlioglu F, Higgins S.
items.abstract: Biomass allocation in plants is mainly interpreted through two major theories: Allometric Partitioning Theory (APT) and Optimal Partitioning Theory (OPT). Under a specific environmental condition where drought and shade co-occur, biomass allocation can also be explained by trade-off, facilitation, and uncoupled hypotheses. These theories and hypotheses make contradictory predictions regarding the direction of biomass allocation to above- versus belowground organs. Because empirical support can be found for each of them, it remains unresolved which framework better explains biomass allocation strategies under combined effects of drought and shade. Moreover, we lack a unified understanding of how these frameworks may integrate. To test these five frameworks, we examined three Fagaceae species with contrasting tolerances: drought-tolerant Quercus pubescens , shade-tolerant Fagus sylvatica , and Castanea sativa with moderate shade and drought tolerance. We conducted a greenhouse experiment to detect seedling responses to simulated drought and shade using an experimental design controlling water-table gradients, light quality and quantity. We analyzed aboveground growth via LiDAR, aboveground/belowground biomass allocations, and resource acquisition strategies of these three species. We found that individual seedling responses were highly nuanced along continuous gradients, and no single theory and hypothesis adequately explained the observed biomass allocation. Moreover, we developed a novel decision chart that systematically links these disparate theories and hypotheses, rather than treating them as mutually exclusive frameworks.

items.title: Regulation of the physicochemical properties, structure, and long-term retrogradation behavior of Lonicera caerulea berry polyphenol-chestnut starch complexes using high hydrostatic pressure.
items.authors: Yang M, Wang X, Chen Y, Lu Z, Liu S, Dong L.
items.abstract: Starch retrogradation affects the quality of starch-based foods. In this study, high hydrostatic pressure (HHP) was used as a nonthermal pretreatment to promote interactions between Lonicera caerulea berry polyphenols (LCBP) and chestnut starch (CS), with particular emphasis on their combined effects on physicochemical, structural, and long-term retrogradation properties over 7 days. HHP treatments at 200, 400, and 600 MPa and LCBP concentrations of 0%, 4%, 8%, and 12% (on a starch dry basis) were evaluated during storage at 4 °C. Based on the complexation index (CI) and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy screening results, the 600 MPa-8% LCBP treatment was selected as the representative combined treatment for detailed characterization. FTIR spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and water separation analyses further showed reduced short-range molecular order, relatively loose porous structures, and improved water retention in HHP-treated LCBP-CS systems during storage. After 7 days of refrigerated storage at 4 °C, compared with untreated CS stored under the same conditions, the 600 MPa-8% LCBP treatment reduced the relative crystallinity and enthalpy of recrystallization by 32.24% and 50.98%, respectively, while increasing the calculated nonhydrolyzed fraction by 66.85% (P < 0.05). Correlation analysis showed that a higher complexation index was associated with lower retrogradation-related indices and rapidly digestible starch content, consistent with greater resistance to long-term retrogradation and in vitro enzymatic digestion. This study provides further insights into the effects of HHP-treated LCBP-CS complexes on long-term retrogradation and in vitro digestion behavior.

items.title: PROGRESSION OF A KNEMIDOCOPTIASIS-LIKE DERMATITIS IN A WILD CHESTNUT-BELLIED SCALED QUAIL (CALLIPEPLA SQUAMATA CASTANOGASTRIS)
items.authors: Levi D. Sweeten, E. Tanner, Alynn M. Martin, Maydeliz Ramos-Gonzalez, Ashley M. Tanner, F. Hernández
items.abstract: La dermatitis aviar abarca una variedad de afecciones que causan irritación e inflamación de la piel en las aves y puede surgir de diversos agentes causales. Los reportes de enfermedades en especies aviares silvestres suelen ser incidentales y aislados, pero proporcionan información de referencia valiosa para la investigación de enfermedades en la vida silvestre. En febrero de 2024, durante un estudio de captura-marcaje-recaptura en Duval, Texas, EE. UU., se capturó una hembra adulta de codorniz escamosa ventricastaña (Callipepla squamata castanogastris) que presentaba síntomas compatibles con dermatitis. Se observaron lesiones hiperqueratósicas en las patas, con reducción parcial de los halluxes. El mismo fue recapturado en mayo de 2024 con síntomas que evidenciaban una mayor gravedad de la enfermedad, incluyendo lesiones más extensas en las patas y piernas, y pérdida de múltiples dedos, tanto total en los posteriores como parcial en los demás. Los intentos por confirmar el agente causal de la enfermedad resultaron infructuosos. Sin embargo, la presentación y la progresión de la enfermedad fueron compatibles con la knemidocoptiasis (sarna aviar), una dermatitis causada por ácaros parásitos que excavan la epidermis sin plumas. Este informe representa uno de los escasos documentos que describen síntomas de dermatitis en codornices silvestres y, hasta donde sabemos, el primer reporte y la primera observación longitudinal de una dermatitis de tipo sarnoso en la codorniz escamosa silvestre.

items.title: Effects of Withering Duration on Quality Characteristics and the Volatile Metabolome of Green Tea and Black Tea from the New Cultivar “Chanjin No. 3”
items.authors: Peng Zeng, Yue Liu, Ke-Xia Zhou, Guo-Xun Li, Xiao Han, Heng-Bin Guo
items.abstract: Withering is a vital preliminary process in determining tea quality. To explore the effects of withering duration (2 h, 6 h, 10 h) on green tea and black tea from the new cultivar “Chanjin No. 3”, leaf moisture dynamics, sensory attributes, pigment profiles, major quality components, and volatile metabolites were systematically evaluated. Leaf relative water content continuously declined with prolonged withering. Sensory evaluation showed that 6 h withering yielded high overall quality for both teas. However, excessive 10 h withering impaired green-tea sensory performance, whereas black tea maintained acceptable quality. Withering exerted distinct regulatory effects on pigment and intrinsic metabolites: 6 h treatment favored theaflavin and theabrownin accumulation in black tea, while overwithering caused substantial total pigment loss. Prolonged withering elevated water extract and soluble sugar contents in black tea, yet reduced water extracts and increased polyphenols in green tea. Gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GC-MS) identified 173 volatile compounds. Withering increased volatile counts and the content of alcohols in green tea and promoted grassy-leaf, floral-honey, and chestnut-nutty aroma substances in black tea. This study indicates that 6 h natural withering is an appropriate option for producing high-quality “Chanjin No. 3” tea and provides processing references for this cultivar.

items.title: Preparation of Humidity-Responsive Thymol Preservative Bags and Application in Storage of Actinidia arguta Fruits ( cv . Longcheng 2)
items.authors: Jing Ma, Xin-Yuan Guo, Xiao-Xuan Liu, Li-Zheng Yi, Qi-Yun He, Ju-Min Hou
items.abstract: A humidity-responsive preservative system enables on-demand release of thymol with moisture changes due to respiration in the storage atmosphere. Accordingly, a humidity-responsive thymol preservative bag was prepared to preserve Actinidia arguta fruits (cv. Longcheng 2). First, thymol was encapsulated into hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD) to form Thymol@HP-β-CD with an encapsulation efficiency of 92.31 ± 4.22%, and it effectively inhibited Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Second, a humidity-responsive PVA film was prepared to wrap the Thymol@HP-β-CD powder for fabricating the preservative bag, which could cumulatively release 83.00 ± 9.54% thymol at 90% relative humidity over 15 days. Lastly, the preservative bag was used in Actinidia arguta fruit (cv. Longcheng 2) storage, which could significantly delay visible decay, effectively protecting the appearance, texture, chlorophyll content, and antioxidant ability. The humidity-responsive preservative bags would have great potential in non-contact fruit storage.

items.title: Predicting Fruit-Drop Severity in ‘Rojo Brillante’ Persimmon: An Ordinal Classification Approach with Implications for Irrigation Scheduling
items.authors: A. Román, P. González-Altozano, L. Bonet, E. Badal, Miquel Llompart, M. A. Martínez-Gimeno
items.abstract: Physiological fruit drop is a major determinant of crop load and yield in ‘Rojo Brillante’ persimmon and is closely linked to irrigation management, yet its severity has not been addressed as an ordinal prediction problem. This study evaluated whether fortnightly fruit-drop severity, recorded in 2015–2019 in trees grafted onto Diospyros lotus and Diospyros virginiana under different irrigation treatments, could be predicted one fortnight in advance with four ordinal classification algorithms (cumulative link model, LogitBoost, random forest and support vector machine). Nested and reduced predictor sets were evaluated with leave-one-year-out cross-validation against a persistence and a seasonal baseline, with Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) as the pre-specified primary metric. LogitBoost with the complete predictor set achieved the highest agreement (QWK = 0.718), outperforming the persistence baseline (QWK = 0.510) in all five years and the seasonal baseline (QWK = 0.591) in four. Reduced models with cumulative growing degree-days and rootstock reached similar agreement, indicating that predictive ability arises mainly from seasonal phase. In contrast, the previous fruit-drop count and additional agroclimatic predictors improved the discrimination of low and moderate drop. Because irrigation enters the models through the cumulative hydric balance, the approach could support the evaluation of irrigation scenarios, once validated in other orchards.

items.title: Genome-wide identification and expression profiling of the 14-3–3 gene family in woodland strawberry (Fragaria vesca) under abiotic stresses and hormone treatments
items.authors: Ting-Ting Fang, Tian-Hong Ni, Chang-Mei Du, Xiang-Xiang Dong, Jian-Hua Yue, Pei-Ling Li
items.abstract: 14-3-3 proteins constitute a highly conserved regulatory protein family in eukaryotes, playing indispensable roles in plant growth, development, and stress responses. Although the 14-3–3 gene family has been characterized in many plant species, its identification and involvement in stress responses remain unexplored in Fragaria vesca . In this study, We identified 14-3–3 genes in three Rosaceae genomes, with 8, 9, and 9 members in Fragaria vesca , Rubus occidentalis , and Prunus davidiana , respectively. Subsequently, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the strawberry gene family, covering their physicochemical properties, phylogeny, chromosomal locations, exon–intron structures, and expression patterns. Multiple sequence alignments and secondary structure predictions of Fv14-3–3 proteins indicated all the members contained nine conserved antiparallel α-helices. Phylogenetic analysis showed that they were categorized into ϵ and non-ϵ groups with four members, respectively. The Fv14-3–3 gene family members were unevenly distributed across the chromosomes, most proteins within each group shared similar conserved motifs, and gene structure analysis showed that gene length and intron number varied greatly among the members within the ϵ group, with FvGF14c having a single-exon structure. Promoter sequence analysis showed that the Fv14-3–3 gene promoters contained more cis-acting elements related to abiotic stress tolerance and phytohormone responses. RNA-seq data showed that Fv14–3–3 genes were expressed in all tissues of strawberry but that their expression patterns were different. items.title: Environmental Influence on Poplar Leaf Traits: Insights from Principal Component Analysis
items.journal: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology
items.authors: D. Ayate, M. Jain, Jaipal Sharma, Sneha Dobhal, Yogesh Yadavrao Sumthane
items.abstract: The present study evaluated variation in leaf morphological traits of Populus deltoides clones grown at three locations: Naganji Nursery, Nauni; RH&TS, Dhaula Kuan; and Ladhowal, PAU, Ludhiana. Fifteen clones were planted in a randomised block design with three replications at each site, and leaf traits were recorded using measurement scales and UPOV guidelines. The assessed traits included leaf blade length, maximum width, the distance from the petiole junction to the point of maximum leaf width, midrib length, petiole length, the distance from the petiole junction to the leaf base, selected trait ratios, total leaf length, leaf area, the angle between the midrib and the second lower lateral vein, and apex angle. Principal component analysis was used to identify traits contributing to total variation across the combined sites. The first three principal components had eigenvalues greater than unity and together explained 90.07% of the total variation. The first component accounted for 56.52% of the variation and was mainly associated with midrib length, leaf blade length, leaf area, total leaf length, maximum width, and the distance from the petiole junction to the point of maximum leaf width. The second component explained 19.35% of the variation and was mainly associated with petiole length and apex angle, whereas the third component explained 14.20% and was influenced by the distance from the petiole junction to the leaf base and the vein angle. These results indicate that leaf size and shape traits are contributors to morphological variation among poplar clones.

items.title: Current status of the fruit industry in beijing based on agricultural big data
items.authors: Zhao-Quan Gao
items.abstract: This study used 2020 agricultural big data to systematically characterise spatial patterns, production performance, marketing channels, and key bottlenecks for the city’s fresh and dried‑fruit industries. In 2020, Beijing’s total area under fruit-tree cultivation reached 125,657 ha. Fresh-fruit orchards were predominantly located in Pinggu, Daxing and Changping Districts, while dried-fruit production was concentrated in Miyun and Huairou Districts. Peaches and chestnuts were the dominant commercial fresh and dried-fruit crops. The city produced 513,800 t of fruit valued at 523.12 million US dollars. Local fruit production could satisfy only a small share of Beijing’s municipal fruit consumption demand. Major limiting factors included low orchard modernisation, suppressed fruit prices, insufficient grower incomes, and imbalanced industrial development across administrative districts. This big-data-driven spatial analysis provides practical references for optimising fruit-tree resource allocation and advancing sustainable fruit-production systems for megacity contexts. Bangladesh J. Bot. 55(3): 659-669, 2026 (September) Special

items.title: Effects of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi on seedling growth and protective enzyme system of actinidia arguta
items.authors: Wen-Quan Zhang, Qian Dai, Li-Hua Li, Ru-Lai He, Lin Zhu, Yan-Ming Wang
items.abstract: A pot experiment was conducted to evaluate the effects of two arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) species, Glomus mosseae (G.m) and G. versiforme (G.v), on the growth, mineral nutrition, photosynthetic performance, and leaf antioxidant enzyme systems of Actinidia arguta seedlings. AMF inoculation significantly enhanced the uptake of N, P and K. Inoculation also substantially improved photosynthetic capacity and elevated the activities of key antioxidant enzymes. G.m inoculation resulted in higher root colonization rates, greater P accumulation, increased chlorophyll concentration, enhanced net photosynthetic rate, and elevated peroxidase (POD) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activities. In contrast, G.v was more effective in increasing N and K contents, as well as catalase (CAT) activity. AMF inoculation is a promising biotechnological approach to promote the growth and physiological performance of A. arguta seedlings. Bangladesh J. Bot. 55(3): 867-871, 2026 (September) Special

items.title: Optimizing Irrigation Salinity for Ziziphus jujuba ‘Dongzao’ Production Through Jujube Yield, Quality and Soil Health in the Yellow River Delta: A Three-Year Field Experiment
items.authors: Yu-Cai Xie, Rong-Zhen Wang, Zheng-He Xu, X. Cong, G. Pang
items.abstract: Brackish water is usually abundant and regarded as a potential irrigation water resource in the Yellow River Delta, China, but may cause soil salt accumulation and potentially compromise crop quality. The tolerable salinity threshold of irrigation water for Ziziphus jujuba ‘Dongzao’ in saline–alkali soil remains uncertain. To use the brackish water safely and effectively, a comprehensive three-year field investigation (2020–2022) was conducted in Zhanhua, Binzhou, utilizing a drip irrigation system under five irrigation water salinity regimes: 1 g·L−1 (control), 2 g·L−1, 3 g·L−1, 4 g·L−1, and 5 g·L−1. The study systematically evaluated the impact of brackish irrigation on the spatiotemporal distribution of soil salinity, jujube physiological traits, yield, and quality to identify the optimal salinity range for enhanced productivity and resource efficiency. Results showed that increasing salt concentration increased soil conductivity (EC1:5), but rainfall reduced EC1:5. Compared to the first sampling conducted in April 2020, due to the increased rainfall in 2021 and 2022, a balance in soil salinity has been achieved within the 0–100 cm soil layer. Higher salt concentrations reduced jujube branch length and fruit yield, with the most significant decreases occurring at concentrations exceeding 4 g·L−1. Specifically, compared to T1, the yields of T2, T3, T4, and T5 decreased by 0.5% to 6.4%, 2.0% to 8.6%, 5.3% to 14.1%, and 12.1% to 20.3%, respectively, over the three-year period. Interestingly, fruit quality improved as salt concentrations increased, reaching an optimum at 4 g·L−1. At a salinity of 3 g·L−1, physiological indicators such as chlorophyll content, photosynthetic and transpiration rates, and quantum efficiency showed improvements compared with 1 g·L−1. However,…

items.title: Identification of the HD-ZIP Transcription Factor Family and Functional Analysis of CmHB40 in Castanea mollissima
items.authors: Yun-He Cheng, Li-Li Cheng, Guang-Long Hu, Qian-Yu Yang, Yan-Ping Lan
items.abstract: Evidence has increasingly shown that the HB53/40/21 clade within HD-ZIP I plays an important role in floral organ development in plants. In this study, we performed genome-wide identification of HD-ZIP family members in Chinese chestnut Castanea mollissima using bioinformatics analysis, cloned the HB53/40/21 homologous gene CmHB40, and analyzed its expression pattern and subcellular localization. Using DAP-seq technology and yeast one-hybrid and dual-luciferase assays, we identified the DNA sequences bound by CmHB40 and its downstream target genes. We also verified the biological function of CmHB40 through heterologous overexpression. Our results demonstrate that CmHB40 shares a conserved molecular structure and DNA-binding capacity with HB53/40/21 homologs from other species. However, in Chinese chestnut, CmHB40 is predominantly expressed in male flowers, where it directly binds to the promoters of pollen exine and cuticular wax biosynthesis genes CmCER1 and CmABCG11, and upregulates their expression. However, overexpression of CmHB40 in Arabidopsisthaliana inhibited petal and stamen development. The expression of GA-related genes AtJUB1 and AtGA2ox2 was upregulated in transgenic individuals. From the above results, we infer that CmHB40 shares a conserved molecular structure with HB53/40/21 homologs from other species. We propose a regulatory model in which CmHB40 participates in flower development by upregulating the expression of CmCER1 and CmABCG11. This inference awaits verification once a genetic transformation system for Chinese chestnut has been established.

items.title: The ZjGRF3-GIF1 chimeric protein boosts leaf disc regeneration and transformation efficiency in jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.).
items.authors: Yuan Y, Yang S, Gao Y, Chen Y, Long C, Zhu X, Li M, Cheng S, Zhang Q, Bo W, Pang X.
items.abstract: An efficient and stable genetic transformation system is essential for functional genomics and molecular breeding of Chinese jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.), yet poor in vitro regeneration remains a major bottleneck in many germplasms. Here, we evaluated the effects of ZjGRF3 and ZjGIF1 using single-gene overexpression constructs, a ZjGRF3-ZjGIF1 fusion construct, and a miR396 target site-mutated fusion construct. The ZjGRF3-ZjGIF1 fusion promoted regeneration more strongly than either gene expressed alone, while mutation of the miR396 recognition site further increased regeneration efficiency to 72.51% and significantly enhanced transformation efficiency. Analysis of callus induction, adventitious shoot production, and regeneration timing showed that all treatments exhibited 100% callus induction, whereas the major differences occurred during subsequent shoot organogenesis. The fusion constructs increased adventitious shoot number per regenerating callus and accelerated shoot emergence, indicating that their principal effect occurred after callus establishment. Transcriptome profiling of stable ZjGRF3-overexpressing plants revealed broad transcriptional changes associated with redox regulation, secondary metabolism, hormone-related processes, membrane transport, cell division, and cellular organization, providing molecular clues potentially related to ZjGRF3 function. Overall, these results demonstrate that the ZjGRF3-ZjGIF1 module effectively enhances jujube regeneration and transformation, and that miR396 target-site modification further strengthens its regeneration-promoting effect. This study provides a practical genetic strategy for improving jujube transformation and offers a basis for further investigation of GRF-mediated regeneration in woody fruit trees.

items.title: Uncertainty-weighted fuzzy clustering disentangles climate-stress VOC fingerprints and associated stress-dependent temperature sensitivity in urban trees
items.authors: Dey B, Depp C, Gu Y, Novelli A, Fuchs H, Hohaus T, Pfannerstill EY.
items.abstract: Abstract Climate change increases the severity and frequency of heat and oxidative stress that plants experience, yet their simultaneous effects on biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) emissions remains poorly understood, complicating the predictability of future air quality and climate. Here, canopy BVOC emissions from linden and chestnut trees were measured over a continuous two-month chamber experiment without stress, heat stress, and combined O₃ and heat stress. To untangle stress-associated BVOC fingerprints, we developed an unsupervised uncertainty-weighted fuzzy c-means (UWFCM) algorithm that directly incorporates compound- and measurement-specific analytical uncertainties into clustering. UWFCM identified monoterpenes (increased up to 3-fold) and sesquiterpenes (up to 22-fold) as the primary heat-stress markers in both species, while increased diterpenes characterized combined O₃ and heat stress in linden. Stress-induced de novo emissions resulted in carbon loss up to ~ 14% of net daytime carbon fixation, a substantial stress-related carbon reallocation. The temperature sensitivity of terpenoid emissions was strongly stress-dependent. These findings have important implications for global BVOC parameterizations, estimates of daytime NO x -driven ozone chemistry and secondary organic aerosol formation under future climate extremes.

items.title: Біологічні особливості шкідника жолудів Cydia splendana (Hübner, 1799) (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae: Olethreutinae: Grapholitini) на Сході України
items.authors: V. Us
items.abstract: Серед комах-карпофагів жолудів дуба в Україні значне місце посідає сіра плодожерка Cydia splendana (Hübner, 1799) (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae), яка відома в Європі як шкід- ник плодів різних видів родів Quercus L., Castanea Mill., Juglans L. Біологічні особливості C. splendana досліджені переважно у південних регіонах Європи на плантаціях каштана їстівного. Збагачення відомостей щодо розвитку плодожерки C. splendana в дубових насадженнях на сході України є актуальним з погляду вдосконалення моніторингу стану та захисту врожаю жолудів під час їхнього розвитку. Метою досліджень було встано- вити деякі особливості сезонного розвитку плодожерки C. splendana в дубових насаджен- нях сходу України. Дослідження проведені у 2023–2026 рр. У дослідах використовували жолуді, зібрані у серпні–жовтні 2023–2025 рр. у дубових насадженнях і полезахисних сму- гах Харківської та Полтавської областей. Встановлено, що середній зважений вік гусе- ниць C. splendana становив IV,2 у серпні, IV,3 у вересні, IV,5 у жовтні та IV,8 – у листопаді. Виліт метеликів C. splendana незалежно від дат і температури відбувався у проміжку від 20:00 до 23:30. Виліт метеликів C. splendana з жолудів, перенесених в опалюване примі- щення 10 жовтня 2024 року, розпочався через 138 днів, а переміщених 2 січня та 14 січня 2025 р. – через 114 і 111 днів відповідно. За одночасного перенесення жолудів у листо- паді 2025 р. із природних умов у опалюване та неопалюване приміщення суми ефектив- них температур (СЕТ) (з порогом 10°С) від початку вильоту до вильоту 50 % метеликів C. splendana, становили 510 і 508°С, до вильоту 90 % метеликів – 850 і 868°С, а до вильоту 100 % метеликів – 1000 і 1021,8°С в опалюваному та неопалюваному примі- щеннях відповідно. У польових умовах у 2024 році літ метеликів C. splendana розпочався у …

items.title: Susceptibility to fungal deterioration of an ancient monoxyl and a medieval shipwreck under postexcavation environmental stress
items.authors: Ivana Đokić, N. Unković, M. Ljaljević-Grbić, Milan Gavrilović, A. Oskolski, P. Janaćković
items.abstract: An archeological discovery, a well-preserved ancient monoxyle dated from the first century BCE to the first century CE and a fifteenth- to seventeenth-century shipwreck, excavated at the Drmno open-pit coal mine, created a unique opportunity for the fungal-induced deterioration of newly excavated archaeological wooden artifacts to be studied in Serbia for the first time. The monoxyle was carved from a single tree trunk of Pinus nigra or Pinus sylvestris , while two shipwreck wooden samples were shown to be Castanea sativa and Quercus (White Oaks group). Despite identical semihypogean conditions favorable for fungal colonization, the artifacts responded differently: the monoxyle showed extensive decay, predominantly by the brown rot fungus Coniophora puteana , with additional symptoms linked to Mortierellaceae and Niesslia sp., while the shipwreck lacked visible damage, although microscopic evidence revealed Niesslia , Cephalotrichum , and other fungi. Based on the documented fungal structures, both objects have, to an extent, shared a deteriogenic mycobiome. Most of the fungi documented on monoxyle and shipwreck are associated with soft rot, or are often linked with decayed wood. Likewise, many observed species are known to be associated with archeological wooden artifacts and to produce an array of lignocellulolytic enzymes, while the up-to-date published literature suggests that this is the first report of soft rot fungi Microascus melanosporus and Pseudogymnoascus sp. being documented on archeological wood. Understanding the site-specific fungal communities and the environmental conditions to which the objects are exposed, and identifying the wood species of artifacts, are crucial, as this information directly informs the selection of appropriate and effective conser…

items.title: Development and validation of a method for quantitative determination of saponins in Aesculus hippocastanum L. flowers
items.authors: A. Dunilin, O. V. Trineeva
items.abstract: Introduction. Saponins are an extensive class of natural glycosides that perform important functions in plant life processes. Horse chestnut ( Aesculus hippocastanum L.), a plant of the genus Aesculus L., family Hippocastanaceae Burnett, is a promising medicinal plant. In official medicine, chestnut seeds are used as a venotonic and capillary-protective agent due to the complex of triterpene saponins contained in them, the main active ingredient of which is the glycoside β-escin. In folk medicine, flowers, leaves, bark, buds and capsules of chestnut are also used. Horse chestnut flowers contain a wide range of biologically active substances (BAS), which makes them a promising type of medicinal plant raw materials (MPRM) with a pronounced therapeutic potential. However, the group of triterpene saponins in their composition remains insufficiently studied. Aim. To develop and validate a spectrophotometric method for determining saponins in horse chestnut flowers, as well as to test it on raw materials from various growing regions to scientifically substantiate raw material quality standards. Materials and methods. The study involved air-dried horse chestnut flowers harvested in the Petrozavodsk urban district, Leningrad, Moscow, Voronezh, and Volgograd regions, and Stavropol Krai during the mass flowering period (May — June) in 2024. To quantify the total saponin content as β-escin, a spectrophotometric method was adapted. This method involves oxidation with concentrated sulfuric acid, accompanied by dehydration, which leads to the formation of colored quinoid structures. Optical density was measured using an SF-2000 spectrophotometer in the wavelength range of 250—450 nm. The method was validated in accordance with the general pharmacopoeial article (PA) "Validation of an…

items.title: Global conservation and utilization of wild pear germplasm resources
items.authors: Hao-Fang Zhao, Hua Xu, Shen Yan, Yu-Nan Lin, B. Pan, Ya-Ning Cao
items.abstract: The wild pear group represents an important genetic resource for improving stress resistance in pear cultivars and for rootstock breeding; however, under global warming, its conservation and utilization remain insufficient. In this study, an integrated framework was introduced that combines habitat prediction, conservation gap analysis, and utilization of wild germplasm. Using the ensemble species distribution models (ESDMs) together with GapAnalysis, global suitable habitat dynamics of the genus Pyrus under four future climate scenarios (2021–2040) were predicted, and conservation gaps were identified. Additionally, a novel BC-RP system was established by integrating the Breeding Contribution Score (BC-score) and mean retention proportion (RP-mean) to jointly assess climatic stability and improvement potential of the wild group. The results reveal that climate warming has caused widespread habitat decline, with 16 wild species classified as urgent conservation priorities. On this basis, six wild species showing climatic stability and potential utilization capacity were identified as promising resources for improving major cultivated pear cultivars. This study exposes critical conservation deficiencies and establishes a scientific foundation for the preservation and sustainable use of the wild group.

items.title: High Throughput Sequencing vs Biological Indexing for the Detection of Viral Pathogens in Rubus.
items.authors: Fager D, Al Rwahnih M, Mollov D.
items.abstract: Rubus species are native to six continents and are grown commercially around the world. Production of raspberries and blackberries in the United States alone is over 100,000 metric tons. Global production and transport require prevention of both endemic and exotic diseases through clean plant programs and certification testing. While graft bioassay has been the standard in certification programs for pathogen detection, high throughput sequencing (HTS) has the potential to streamline the testing process and identify pathogens more effectively. In this study, HTS was evaluated for virus detection compared to graft bioassay in Rubus plants. Leaves from 71 donor plants were grafted onto three replicates of Rubus occidentalis 'Munger' black raspberry indicator plants and monitored for symptom expression over eight weeks and again after natural winter dormancy. Donor leaves were analyzed by HTS for the presence of viral sequences. The experiment was repeated twice with six replicates per donor plant across both experiments and 426 indicators total. HTS detected 20 virus species across all donors with up to six viruses in a single plant. Virus detection by HTS and graft bioassay did not correlate well. HTS detected viruses in 100% of donors while 45% of grafted indicators were asymptomatic by eight weeks after grafting and 61% asymptomatic after dormancy. Results indicate HTS is more effective at detecting viral infections, even when grafted plants are subject to natural dormancy.

items.title: Physiological and biochemical responses of chestnut cultivars to drought and rewatering
items.authors: Marques T, Ferreira-Pinto A, Pinto T, Gomes-Laranjo J.
items.abstract: Abstract Drought is an increasingly important constraint for chestnut cultivation in Mediterranean regions, where recurrent summer water deficits can restrict plant performance and compromise recovery after stress release. In Castanea sativa Mill., drought resilience depends on the coordinated adjustment of physiological and biochemical traits rather than on the behaviour of a single marker. This study evaluated three Portuguese chestnut cultivars, Judia, Longal, and Martaínha, grafted onto CA-90 rootstock, together with non-grafted CA-90 plants, under controlled drought and rewatering conditions. Plants were assessed at the initial irrigated phase (IP), after 7 days of irrigation withdrawal (NIP), and after 30 days of rewatering (RIP). Net photosynthesis, transpiration, leaf temperature, soluble sugars, starch, soluble proteins, electrolyte leakage, catalase (CAT), ascorbate peroxidase (APX), total phenolic compounds, total flavonoids, and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) were analysed. Drought reduced gas exchange in all plant materials and increased leaf temperature, indicating marked functional impairment under water deficit. Longal and Martaínha maintained comparatively higher physiological performance during drought and showed the strongest recovery after rewatering, whereas CA-90 displayed the lowest gas-exchange rates, greater starch depletion, and higher membrane damage. Soluble sugars, soluble proteins, CAT, and APX increased during drought, while starch declined in all cultivars. In contrast, phenolics, flavonoids, and FRAP decreased under water deficit and recovered partially or substantially after rewatering. items.title: Unveiling the Chemical Signature of Abruzzo Bee Pollen: Markers of Authenticity, Bioactive Phytochemicals and Antioxidant Activity
items.authors: Chiara Collevecchio, F. Epifano, S. Genovese, Serena Fiorito
items.abstract: Bee pollen is a complex natural matrix rich in bioactive compounds, a valuable source with high nutritional value. Its chemical composition is highly variable and is influenced by botanical origin and geographical area, posing significant challenges for quality control and authentication. In this study, the volatile and semi-volatile fingerprints of Abruzzo bee pollen samples were investigated by HS–GC–MS and GC–MS, enabling the identification of 61 compounds. GC–MS profiling revealed distinct chemical patterns among the investigated bee-pollen samples, with multifloral samples (MP7–MP13) and chestnut pollen (CP1–CP2) showing a similar profile associated with the occurrence of linoleic acid. Moreover, the aldehydic volatile fingerprint further contributed potential chemical markers of botanical and territorial origin, particularly hexanal and nonanal, which may represent characteristic volatile markers of this botanical source, while 3-methylbutanal as well as sulphureous compounds contributed to the distinctive volatile profile of MP1 and MP2. These latter exhibited a distinctive phytochemical profile characterized by umbelliferon (UMB) and 7-isopentenyloxycoumarin (7-IPC), compounds with recognized bioactive properties that may contribute to the functional value of bee pollen. Antioxidant capacity was evaluated using ABTS and DPPH radical scavenging assays. The highest antioxidant activity was observed in MP1 and MP2, potentially reflecting the contribution of oxyprenylated coumarins. The presence of these coumarin derivatives may also provide insights into the botanical origin of the samples and their potential chemotaxonomic relevance. Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed clear chemical distinctions associated with botanical origin, effectively discriminating…

items.title: A novel partitivirus induces hypovirulence and increases pyraclostrobin sensitivity in the phytopathogenic fungus <i>Lasiodiplodia ziziphi</i>.
items.authors: Wang Y, Gao X, Xie S, Guo Y, Wu H, Zhou F, Yu H, Zhang M.
items.abstract: Lasiodiplodia ziziphi causes canker disease in jujube and other woody plants. Its control relies mainly on fungicides. Mycoviruses that cause hypovirulence are an emerging option for the biological control of fungal diseases. In this study, we identified a novel double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) mycovirus, Lasiodiplodia ziziphi partitivirus 1 (LzPV1), from L. ziziphi strain CDZM004. The LzPV1 genome consists of two dsRNA segments. dsRNA1 (1,905 bp) encodes an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), and dsRNA2 (1,773 bp) encodes a capsid protein (CP). The genome is packaged into isometric virions about 32 nm in diameter. Phylogenetic analysis of the RdRp and CP placed LzPV1 in the genus Alphapartitivirus of the family Partitiviridae. LzPV1 was transmitted horizontally through hyphal anastomosis and vertically through conidia. LzPV1 infection reduced the virulence of L. ziziphi, changed its hyphal morphology, and increased fungal sensitivity to the fungicide pyraclostrobin. This is the first mycovirus reported in L. ziziphi and the first partitivirus described in the genus Lasiodiplodia. LzPV1 is a promising biocontrol resource for jujube canker disease.

items.title: Protective Effects of Ziziphus jujuba Mill. Leaves Against Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Are Associated with Gut Microbiota and Hepatic Metabolic Remodeling
items.authors: Tian-Shuo Zhang, Dong-Sheng Jia, Hui-Yi Zhang, Guang-Zhao Zhou, Jie Liu, Jia-Tian Gu
items.abstract: Background: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent chronic liver disorder with limited effective pharmacological treatments. Ziziphus jujuba Mill. leaves (ZJL) contain multiple bioactive compounds, but their effects on MASLD and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods: The chemical constituents of ethanolic ZJL extract were characterized using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap MS. A high-fat diet (HFD)-induced MASLD mouse model was used to evaluate its protective effects. Serum biochemical parameters, liver histopathology, and inflammatory indicators were assessed. Gut microbiota and hepatic metabolic alterations were investigated using 16S rDNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics, respectively. Potential microbiota–metabolite associations and key regulatory targets were further explored by correlation analysis, molecular docking, and qRT-PCR. Results: Fifty-five compounds were identified in ZJL, mainly flavonoids, organic acids, and triterpenoids. ZJL treatment significantly reduced HFD-induced body weight gain, dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, hepatic injury, inflammation, and lipid accumulation. ZJL also partially restored gut microbial homeostasis, particularly by decreasing the abundances of Blautia and Dorea. Metabolomic analysis indicated that glycerophospholipid metabolism was the major affected pathway, together with fatty acid biosynthesis and cytochrome P450-related metabolism. Microbial alterations were closely associated with lipid-related metabolites. Moreover, ZJL downregulated key genes, including Pla2g2a, Fasn, and Cyp2e1. Conclusions: ZJL alleviated HFD-induced MASLD, accompanied by coordinated alterations in gut microbiota composition, hepatic metabolism, and lipid-related gene expression, suggesting that these changes may…

items.title: Multi-omics analyses reveal dynamic interactions between DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation during black raspberry ripening.
items.authors: Hsieh WH, Hung YH, Zhang JH, Cui Q, Chen HY, Lin LP, He MH, Wang YC, Ho YY, Ballington J, Fernandez G, Perkins-Veazie P, H Le B, Li X, Hsieh TF, Lin JY.
items.abstract: Fruit ripening is a complex developmental process involving coordinated changes in gene expression, metabolism, and epigenetic regulation. How DNA methylation dynamics influence gene transcription and metabolite accumulation during black raspberry (Rubus occidentalis) fruit ripening remains poorly understood. Here, we performed developmental-series transcriptome, methylome, and metabolome analysis; the results from this analysis reveal extensive epigenetic reprogramming during black raspberry fruit ripening. Fruit tissues exhibit globally higher DNA methylation than leaves, particularly in CHG and CHH contexts. Local methylation in all cytosine contexts progressively decreases in promoter regions during ripening, whereas CHG and CHH methylation increase in transposon-rich regions. Two primary methylation transitions-promoter hypomethylation and CHH hypermethylation-govern transcriptional shifts in genes involved in ripening processes. Methyl-binding transcription factors with activation potential likely promote CHH hypermethylation-linked transcriptional activation. Multi-omics integration reveals that coordinated anthocyanin accumulation parallels expression of biosynthetic and regulatory genes within coherent networks. Elevated non-CG methylation in heterochromatin coincides with increased transcription of histone variants mediating chromatin compaction, suggesting chromatin remodelers fine-tune accessibility for methyltransferases. Our study highlights both genome-wide and locus-specific epigenetic reprogramming and demonstrates a coordinated interplay between DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation during black raspberry fruit ripening.

items.title: Effects of Saccharomyces boulardii Fermentation on Free and Bound Phenolics, In Vitro Bioaccessibility, Antidiabetic and ACE Inhibitory Activities of Chestnut Inner Shell
items.authors: Sevda Dere, Oznur Saroglu, F. Bozkurt, A. Karadag, O. Sağdıç
items.abstract: Chestnut inner shell (CIS) is a phenolic-rich by-product with potential for valorization through microbial fermentation. This study investigated the effects of autoclaving and subsequent fermentation with Saccharomyces boulardii S10 on free and bound phenolics, antioxidant activity, and α-glucosidase, α-amylase, and angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory activities. Furthermore, simulated in vitro gastrointestinal digestion was performed to evaluate phenolic bioaccessibility and changes in individual phenolic compounds during digestion. Autoclaving increased free total phenolic content (TPC) from 139.09 to 178.61 mg GAE/g DW. During fermentation, the free phenolic fraction exhibited the highest TPC at 48 h (190.81 mg GAE/g DW), accompanied by the lowest TPC in the bound fraction (34.89 mg GAE/g DW). Similarly, α-glucosidase inhibitory activity was highest at 48 h (IC50 = 21.44 µg/mL), whereas ACE inhibitory activity progressively increased throughout fermentation, reaching its maximum at 72 h (IC50 = 10.08 µg/mL). Following in vitro gastrointestinal digestion, gallic and ellagic acid concentrations increased during the intestinal phase. Notably, the 48 h fermented sample exhibited the highest intestinal TPC (218.86 ± 5.02 mg GAE/g DW) among all samples, along with the highest TPC-based bioaccessibility (96.97%) and individual phenolics-based bioaccessibility (16.93%) among the fermented samples. These findings highlight the potential of fermentation to modify phenolic distribution and bioactivities while demonstrating the importance of gastrointestinal digestion in evaluating the bioaccessibility of CIS phenolics.

items.title: Antifungal effect of Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 on postharvest internal decay of chestnut and its potential antifungal mechanisms.
items.authors: Gao Y, Wang P, Zhang Y, Tian Y, Yang Y, Song F, Cheng S, Zheng L, Yan A.
items.abstract: Chestnut Inner Rot Disease (CIRD), a serious postharvest disease caused by multiple fungal pathogens, leads to substantial economic losses in the chestnut industry. Microbial biocontrol offers a safe and effective strategy. In this study, targeting four dominant CIRD pathogenic strains previously isolated, a bacterial strain identified as Bacillus velezensis BLS-7 was isolated from chestnut-cultivated soil. BLS-7 exhibited strong antifungal activity against Diaporthe phaseolorum, Colletotrichum siamense, Fusarium culmorum, and Lasiodiplodia theobromae, with inhibition rates of 84.51% to 96.89%. Moreover, it demonstrated broad-spectrum antagonism against 14 tested pathogenic fungi, all with inhibition rates exceeding 64%. In vivo assays further verified the significant biocontrol efficacy of BLS-7 across different chestnut varieties. Whole-genome sequencing analysis revealed that the BLS-7 genome harbors 13 gene clusters associated with secondary metabolite synthesis. Through headspace solid-phase microextraction combined with Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) of BLS-7 were analyzed, identifying hexyl butyrate as a candidate key inhibitory monomer. This compound inhibited three of the four CIRD pathogens by over 80% in vitro and all four in chestnut assays, with maximum inhibition rates of 82.95% and 75.3%, respectively. Both the VOCs and hexyl butyrate produced by BLS-7 suppressed mycelial growth and sporulation by disrupting hyphal morphology. VOCs and hexyl butyrate also restricted fungal spread on chestnuts and delayed fruit quality deterioration. This work proposes a fumigation-mediated VOC strategy using hexyl butyrate as a candidate key effector against multi-pathogen chestnut rot, offering a promising appr…

items.title: <i>In vitro</i> efficacy of BLAD against <i>Phytophthora cinnamomi</i>: Effects on mycelial growth, sporulation, and zoospore germination of isolates from <i>Quercus suber</i> and <i>Castanea sativa</i>.
items.authors: Trindade M, Machado H, Ferreira RB.
items.abstract: Phytophthora cinnamomi Rands is a devastating soilborne oomycete responsible for root rot in Quercus suber L., Castanea sativa Mill., Quercus ilex L. and many other species worldwide, causing widespread forest decline across Mediterranean ecosystems. The BLAD-containing oligomer (BCO), isolated from Lupinus albus L. cotyledons, is a β-conglutin derived polypeptide oligomer who´s major 20.4 kDa polypeptide BLAD has been reported to exhibit potent and broad-spectrum antifungal and anti-oomycete activity, as well as protective efficacy against P. cinnamomi under greenhouse conditions. However, whether this protection reflects direct pathogen inhibition, host biostimulation or host boosting defense effects remains unresolved, and no in vitro characterization of its anti-P. cinnamomi activity had ever been established. Here, the in vitro activity of a BCO-based commercial formulation (PROBLAD®) was evaluated against five P. cinnamomi isolates (four from Q. suber, one from C. sativa) across multiple endpoints: mycelial radial growth, dry weight, chlamydospore and sporangia production, and zoospore germination. BCO inhibited radial growth in a concentration- and time-dependent manner (EC50: 4.74-6.43 mL/L). At ≥5 mL/L, colonies showed reduced compactness confirmed by dry weight (EC50: 2.63-4.08 mL/L), demonstrating that radial growth underestimates inhibitory activity by not capturing reductions in mycelial density. A transient stimulatory effect (hormesis) was observed at 1-2 mL/L across all isolates. Chlamydospore and sporangia production were fully suppressed at 1-5 mL/L, indicating interference with the induction phase of sporulation. Zoospore germination was inhibited with an EC50 of 5.72 mL/L and completely abolished at 20 mL/L. Microscopic examination revealed progressi…

items.title: The Gibberellin-Responsive Module RsRGL3a-RsGID1b-1-RsATL56 Orchestrates Parthenocarpic Fruit Formation in Seedless Chestnut Rose (Rosa sterilis).
items.authors: Zhou K, Leng Y, Shen L, Min Y, Wen S, Wang Y, Deng L, Peng L, Wang H, Zhong S, Ao Y, Song Z, Yang K, Qiao G, Wen X.
items.abstract: Seedlessness is a fruit trait highly favoured by consumers, with parthenocarpy serving as an important means to achieve seedless fruit. In this work, RsGID1b‐1 responds to GAs and promotes parthenocarpic fruitsetting by activating RsATL56 transcription in seedless chestnut rose ( Rosa sterilis ). RsRGL3a antagonizes RsGID1b‐1 and represses RsATL56 , negatively regulating parthenocarpy.

items.title: Blue Foods of Bihar: Why Its Aquatic Economy Needs an Intelligence Layer
items.authors: Mohan S, Matolia J, Verma S.
items.abstract: Bihar's blue food economy, built on inland fisheries, makhana (fox nut) cultivation, and water chestnut (singhara) farming, is a major contributor to India's aquatic food production and a critical source of rural livelihoods, nutrition, and income. The state ranks fourth among India's inland fish producers, contributes roughly 90% of India's makhana output, and accounts for nearly 60% of the country's water chestnut production. Despite this scale, the sector faces mounting structural risks: climate variability, recurring floods and droughts, rising temperatures, water quality degradation, and disease outbreaks. These risks are compounded by a lack of integrated early-warning systems for water quality and climate monitoring, leaving farmers to react to visible losses rather than anticipate them. This paper reviews the current state of Bihar's three major blue food systems, their production trends, climatic and environmental requirements, and value chain challenges. The paper then presents Twingills, an AI-powered digital twin platform built on NatureDots' AquaNurch Foundation Model, as a proposed intelligence layer to close this gap through real-time and predictive intelligence at farm and landscape scales, forecasting, and timely decision support for farmers and other stakeholders.

items.title: Development and Characterization of Chitosan and Alginate Films Containing Kraft and Organosolv Lignin Nanoparticles for Active Food Packaging
items.authors: Justyna Jakubska, Abdullah, W. Pakieła, K. Gołombek, T. Warski, L. Hawełek
items.abstract: This study examines the effects of kraft and organosolv lignin nanoparticles on chitosan- and sodium alginate-based films designed for active food packaging. Glycerol-plasticized films containing chestnut extract and different nanolignin concentrations were evaluated for their properties and activities. Alginate films generally showed higher tensile strength, reaching 109.35 MPa with 0.2 g of kraft nanolignin, whereas chitosan films provided a better water-vapor barrier, with a minimum permeability of 0.031 mg·µm·Pa−1·s−1·m−2 at 0.02 g of kraft nanolignin. Kraft nanolignin exhibited smaller characteristic structures and produced finer surface features. Organosolv nanolignin formed larger aggregates and generally reduced water absorption. All films decreased light transmission and exhibited antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, with kraft-containing formulations showing the strongest overall inhibition. Spectroscopic, structural, and thermal analyses confirmed intermolecular interactions and slightly improved thermal stability after nanolignin incorporation. All formulations underwent hydrolytic mass loss in phosphate-buffered saline. These findings demonstrate that the matrix, nanolignin type, and concentration can be selected to tailor film properties for specific food-packaging applications.

items.title: Comparative Genomic Insights into Pathogenicity of Diaporthe amygdali and D. eres Associated with Pear Canker in Korea
items.authors: H. Noh, K. Lee, Seong Hwan Kim
items.abstract: Diaporthe species are important fungal pathogens associated with canker and dieback diseases of woody plants, but genomic factors underlying differences in pathogenicity among pear-associated species remain poorly understood. In this study, D. amygdali DUCC20226 and D. eres DUCC15256 were isolated from canker-affected Asian pear (Pyrus pyrifolia) in Korea, representing the first reports of both species causing pear canker in the country. Pathogenicity assays showed that both isolates caused disease symptoms on pear seedlings. High-quality genome assemblies were generated for D. amygdali (49.82 Mb) and D. eres (61.16 Mb), with BUSCO completeness of 98.9% and 98.7%, respectively. Comparative genomic analysis revealed substantial genomic conservation, although strain-specific genes included predicted secreted proteins and candidate effectors. In D. amygdali, two strain-specific candidate effectors potentially associated with necrosis induction were identified. In contrast, D. eres was predicted to possess more carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes, 961 vs. 863) and biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs, 116 vs. 87) than D. amygdali. Mitochondrial genomes differed markedly in size, measuring 49,922 bp in D. amygdali and 93,346 bp in D. eres, despite conserved core gene composition. Phylogenetic analysis based on 15 mitochondrial protein-coding genes placed both strains within Diaporthaceae. These results provide genomic resources for pear-associated Diaporthe species and insights into potential genetic factors underlying pathogenic specialization.

items.title: Actinidia arguta: Organ-Specific Phytochemistry and Biotechnological Applications—A Review
items.authors: G. Melyan, P. Latocha, N. Sahakyan
items.abstract: Actinidia arguta Miq., commonly known as kiwiberry or hardy kiwifruit, is increasingly recognized as a multifunctional horticultural species with nutritional, phytochemical, and biotechnological value. Although research has traditionally focused on fruit quality, increasing evidence indicates that leaves, shoots, stems, roots, flowers, seeds, and processing residues contain diverse metabolites with potential applications in food, nutraceuticals, and biomass valorization. This review provides an integrated, organ-oriented analysis of the phytochemical composition, metabolic specialization, molecular regulation, biotechnological potential, and translational applications of A. arguta. Fruits are important sources of vitamin C, soluble sugars, organic acids, dietary fiber, actinidin, and polyphenols, whereas vegetative tissues accumulate phenolics, flavonoids, hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives, and pentacyclic triterpenoids. Seeds represent a lipid-rich compartment characterized by polyunsaturated fatty acids, particularly α-linolenic acid, as well as tocopherols and other lipophilic compounds. Floral tissues contribute diverse volatile metabolites, while processing residues provide additional sources of dietary fiber and bioactive compounds. Recent metabolomic, transcriptomic, and molecular studies reveal substantial effects of genotype, organ identity, developmental stage, and environmental conditions on phytochemical variation. Despite substantial progress, important gaps remain in multi-organ metabolomic characterization, standardization, bioavailability, safety assessment, and clinical validation. Overall, A. arguta can be considered a whole-plant resource with applications spanning functional foods, nutraceuticals, biotechnology, and sustainable biomass valorization.

items.title: Role of Solvent Polarity in the Extraction and Electrochemical Behavior of Antioxidants From <i>Ziziphus jujuba</i> Leaves.
items.authors: Kalsoom U, Hussain Z, Khan S, Ahmad N, Azizi S, Maaza M.
items.abstract: Ziziphus jujuba is a medicinal plant known for its rich content of antioxidants including flavonoids, saponins, phenolics, and triterpenoids. This study determines the effect of solvent polarity on the extraction yield and investigates phytochemical distribution of the extracts and its electrochemical behavior. Reflux extraction was used for the preparation of crude extracts, using methanol, ethanol, and water. The ethanolic extract was selected for solvent fractionation, using n-hexane, dichloromethane, chloroform, and ethyl acetate. Among the extraction solvents, ethanol produced the highest crude yield (6.0% w/w). Following solvent-solvent fractionation, the ethyl acetate fraction showed the highest recovery among all fractions (0.30% w/w). The presence of flavonoid and saponin fractions was confirmed by phytochemical screening. The highest absorbance was observed in ethyl acetate fraction through UV visible spectrophotometric analysis, A = 0.711 for flavonoids at 415 nm and 0.330 for saponin at 406 nm. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) for ethyl acetate and chloroform fractions showed oxidation peaks at 0.50 V (vs. Ag/AgCl). Fourier transformed infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) analyzed functional groups of flavonoids and saponins. Liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) identified major flavonoids, that is, vicenin II, spinosin, kaemferol (glycoside), and saponins (jujubosides). The result stated that the polarity of solvents plays a vital role in extracting redox-active antioxidants from the leaves of Z. jujuba. Furthermore, it stated that ethyl acetate is the most effective fractionation solvent. This study gives analytical framework for extraction and characterization of antioxidant-rich fraction of Z. jujuba leaves along with emphasis on the role of solvent polarity …
